rationale: Branch-map coverage is complete and faithful: every notebook scientific endpoint is preserved — consolidated load (value_counts + shape), QC metrics with mt/ribo/hb flags and log1p variants (violin + joint scatter), permissive filtering (min_genes=100 / min_cells=3), Scrublet with batch_key="sample" (doublet_score/predicted_doublet), counts-layer save + median normalize_total + log1p, HVG (n_top_genes=2000, batch_key="sample") with dispersion plot, PCA with variance-ratio plot and sample/pct_counts_mt panels, default neighbors + UMAP colored by sample, Leiden (igraph, n_iterations=2) plus resolutions 0.02/0.50/2.00, all QC/doublet re-assessment UMAPs, both duplicated resolution-comparison plots exported separately, both curated marker-gene dotplots, the cell_type_lvl1 mapping, full Wilcoxon rank_genes_groups table for all clusters, the top-5 DE dotplot, the cluster-7 top-5 extraction and top-gene UMAP, and the final annotated AnnData (h5ad + obs CSV). The source diff is export-only plus the /inputs fetch staging: no parameters, formulas, labels, seeds, algorithms or ordering were changed; no errors are suppressed; no branches skipped; no precomputed answers injected; setup performs no analysis; the two h5 inputs are verified byte-identical (MD5 + SHA-256). The one blocking problem is coherence of the offline design: the diff retains the original `EXAMPLE_DATA.load_registry_from_doi()` call, which is a live network dependency (pooch resolves the DOI via doi.org/figshare on every invocation; nothing in setup pre-populates a form that lets it succeed offline). This directly contradicts the worker's own requirement that "the reference run must not call the pooch DOI registry or any DOI URL" and the stated justification for the offline fetch wrapper. If the reference executes in the offline environment the staging was built for, the run crashes before any data is loaded; if network is available, the call is benign but violates the stated offline/determinism contract. Accordingly the input staging must be extended to cover this call (e.g., drop/replace the pooch create+registry-load block with the staged loader, documented as input staging), not patch it with try/except. Minor non-blocking notes: source_evidence cell-number citations drift from the actual notebook cell indices (e.g., neighbors cited as "code cell 43" instead of 34), and excluded_outputs mentions a "/outputs/final/analysis.py" that is not part of the artifact map — documentation sloppiness only.

The only non-export source change is the rebinding of EXAMPLE_DATA to a staged local loader returning the checksum-verified /inputs copies — a permitted input-staging/path change that leaves the read bytes identical.

The added _save_* calls are pure exports of existing results (to_csv/to_json/savefig/write_h5ad) and do not mutate analysis state; the DE export loop only re-reads adata.uns via sc.get.rank_genes_groups_df.
setup_or_export_problems: The diff retains `EXAMPLE_DATA.load_registry_from_doi()` from the original source. This call performs live network resolution of the DOI through doi.org/figshare on every invocation; the setup script stages only the h5 files and the figshare article JSON under /work/cache — it does not seed the pooch registry cache in a way that makes this call succeed offline. It contradicts the plan's own stated requirement that the reference run must not call the pooch DOI registry or any DOI URL, and if the run is offline as the staging design assumes, the script fails before reading any data. Revision: extend the input staging to this call (replace the pooch.create + load_registry_from_doi block with the staged local loader, documented as input staging), rather than wrapping it in try/except (which would suppress errors).
